scientific_question: Do target-dominated Kamil white-glass samples M23, L04 or L09 contain Au-Ag-Cu-rich microdomains that are chemically and morphologically inconsistent with meteoritic Fe-Ni-Co-Ga-Ge contamination and, if present, are any such domains spatially associated with construction-material markers?

priority_samples.reason: clean white glass; ~99.9 wt% SiO2; low Ni/Co; Au and Ag not reported in key bulk table
independent clean white glass; ~99.4 wt% SiO2; low Ni/Co; Au and Ag not reported in key bulk table
white SiO2-rich impactite; described as projectile-poor/Ni below detection in later work; retains large quartz relics and has been repeatedly studied microscopically

white glass with dark coating contamination control

frozen_measurement_sequence: NON_DESTRUCTIVE_IMAGING: micro-CT or equivalent high-resolution X-ray tomography to locate high-density inclusions and foil/sheet/wire/seam-like morphology
ELEMENTAL_MAPPING: micro-XRF or equivalent map for Au, Ag, Cu, Ni, Co, Fe, Ca, S, Al, K, Na, Mg; add Ga, Ge, Pt, Ir where instrumental sensitivity allows
MORPHOLOGY_AND_PHASE: SEM-BSE plus EDS on any high-Z or morphologically anomalous inclusion
TRACE_CONFIRMATION: LA-ICP-MS and/or micro-PIXE on Au-Ag-Cu-Pt-Ir-Os-Ru plus Ni-Co-Ga-Ge; preserve spatial registration to the imaged microdomain
MATRIX_CONTROL: compare same microdomain against adjacent white glass and target-rock controls for Ca-S-Mg and feldspar/granite-style Al-K-Na-Si plus accessory Ti-Zr-Ba-Sr markers

gold_branch: no proportional Fe-Ni-Co-Ga-Ge co-enrichment expected from projectile contamination
worked morphology preferred: foil, sheet, wire, flattened edge, repeated thickness, seam or solder-like zone
matrix_branch: same or spatially linked microdomain shows Ca-S-Mg carbonate/mortar vector OR Al-K-Na-Si feldspar/granite vector with suitable accessory elements
must exceed local Kamil quartzarenite/weathering controls
candidate_rule.coupled_candidate: gold_branch AND matrix_branch in a spatially linked microdomain

conventional_nulls: impact-induced metal/glass phase separation and fractionation
pre-impact weathered surface layer and ordinary lithophile heterogeneity
single rounded metal droplet without worked morphology

outreach_email_draft.subject: Question on Kamil white-glass samples M23, L04 and L09: Au-Ag microdomain re-analysis
outreach_email_draft.body:
Dear Prof. Folco and Prof. D'Orazio,

I am following the published geochemical and petrographic work on Kamil crater impact glasses and would like to ask a narrowly defined sample/data question. In the published bulk data for target-dominated white glass, samples such as M23 and L04 are extremely SiO2-rich and have low Ni-Co relative to projectile-rich dark glass, but Au and Ag are not reported in the key bulk table. L09 is also especially interesting as a projectile-poor white SiO2-rich impactite that has been repeatedly studied microscopically.

Could you please let me know whether M23, L04 and L09, or polished sections/chips from them, are still retained and potentially available for re-analysis, and whether any unpublished Au or Ag measurements already exist for these samples or closely matched white-glass material?

The proposed test would be deliberately conservative and begin non-destructively: locate any high-density micro-inclusions, then map Au-Ag-Cu against Ni-Co-Fe and relevant matrix elements. Only if a reproducible anomalous microdomain were found would follow-up SEM-BSE/EDS and, if appropriate, LA-ICP-MS or micro-PIXE be considered. The main discriminator would be whether any Au-Ag-Cu-rich domain lacks proportional meteoritic Ni-Co-Ga-Ge enrichment and whether its morphology/adjacent matrix can be explained by ordinary target geology, weathering or impact fractionation.

I am not assuming an archaeological interpretation; the immediate goal is simply to determine whether the existing Kamil white-glass collection contains any chemically distinct pre-impact metal microdomains that deserve closer study.

If useful, I can send a one-page frozen analysis protocol with the exact control hierarchy (M23 -> L04 -> L09; L03/L08 contamination controls; L06 projectile-rich positive control; M26/L13/M27 target-rock controls).

Thank you for your time and for the Kamil work.

Best regards,
Hawkar
